core.big_idea: God creates and acts by His reliable word.

passages.reading_note: Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.
Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Cycle 2 opens by revisiting creation through God’s dependable word

claims.statement: Genesis repeatedly presents God speaking and creation responding to His word.
Psalm 33 connects creation with the LORD’s spoken word and reverence for Him.
Together these passages support teaching God’s word as powerful and trustworthy without turning every personal expectation into a promise from God.

core.interpretation_skill: Retell sequence; identify cause and effect; connect to the big story without forced symbolism

learning.foundation_objective: Retell the main action in Genesis 1:1-31; Psalm 33:6-9 and state in simple language that god creates and acts by his reliable word.
learning.extension_objective: Place this event in the Bible's big story and name one concrete way to trust, thank, obey, or care for others in response.
know: God creates and acts by His reliable word.
understand: Meaning depends on immediate context, genre, and available evidence.
Direct observation should remain distinct from synthesis, inference, framework position, prudential judgment, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before interpretation.
Choose one thing in creation, thank God for it, and read one sentence showing God making or ordering the world.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

ask: What does the text directly say?

zero_prep_card.do: Complete God Said / God Made Sequence.
zero_prep_card.close: Restate the big idea and pray.

activities.title: God Said / God Made Sequence
steps: Read the selected evidence and record direct observations.
Place observations and interpretations into the resource categories.
Discuss which conclusions require more than direct textual wording.
Write one careful response that follows from the evidence.
activities.learning_link: Makes evidence classification and formation visible.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw the categories on blank paper or complete verbally.

activities.title: Evidence Class Check
steps: Classify each as text observation, synthesis, inference, framework position, prudential judgment, or application.
Return to the evidence and justify each classification.

flow.instructions: Connect this lesson to something already learned in Cycle 2.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the evidence, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
